2609.10939.title: Evaluating Scaffolding-Oriented Multi-Agent Large Language Model System for Clinical Interview Training
2609.10939.paper_summary: Clinical education must prepare medical students to conduct safe and coherent patient interviews under conditions of uncertainty. Traditional standardized patient (SP) training is resource-intensive and difficult to scale. We developed a scaffolding-oriented multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) AI Standardized Patient (AI-SP) training platform1. The system includes a patient agent for simulated dialog, a tutor agent providing Socratic prompts without disclosing diagnostic information, and a turn-level evaluator agent that monitors clinical progress without revealing summative scores. In a randomized controlled study (N = 100 medical students), participants were assigned to either a multi-agent (MA) scaffolding condition or a control condition. All students completed two learning sessions under their assigned condition followed by an examination conducted in a patient only environment. Performance was assessed using a standardized Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) based rubric. While no significant difference was observed in final diagnostic accuracy between groups, the multi-agent AI standardized patient system improved final examination scores compared to the control group utilizing structured progressive information disclosure; the most substantial and consistent improvements were observed in communication, the expression of empathy, and specific history-taking behaviors. These findings suggest that specialized LLM agents enhance the process quality of simulated clinical interviews without artificially inflating examination outcomes. To support future research, we release a multi-expert annotated dataset comprising transcripts, checklist annotations, turn-level evaluations, and OSCE-aligned scoring outcomes. This resource aims to facilitate the development of pedagogically grounded AI-SP systems and advance research on AI-supported clinical reasoning training.
2609.10939.paper_summary_zh: 臨床教育必須準備醫學生在不確定的情況下進行安全且連貫的病人訪談。傳統的標準化病人（SP）訓練資源密集且難以擴展。我們開發了一個以支架為導向的多代理大型語言模型（LLM）人工智慧標準化病人（AI-SP）訓練平台。該系統包括一個用於模擬對話的病人代理、一個提供蘇格拉底式提示而不透露診斷信息的導師代理，以及一個在不透露總結分數的情況下監控臨床進展的回合級評估代理。在一項隨機對照研究（N = 100名醫學生）中，參與者被分配到多代理（MA）支架條件或控制條件。所有學生在其分配的條件下完成了兩次學習會議，隨後進行了一次僅在病人環境中的考試。表現是使用標準化的客觀結構化臨床考試（OSCE）基準進行評估。雖然在最終診斷準確性方面未觀察到組間的顯著差異，但多代理AI標準化病人系統在最終考試分數上相較於利用結構性漸進信息披露的控制組有所改善；在溝通、表達同理心和特定的病史採集行為方面觀察到最顯著且一致的改善。這些發現表明，專門的LLM代理提高了模擬臨床訪談的過程質量，而不會人為地提高考試結果。為了支持未來的研究，我們發布了一個多專家註釋數據集，包括逐字稿、檢查清單註釋、回合級評估和與OSCE對齊的評分結果。這一資源旨在促進以教育為基礎的AI-SP系統的發展，並推進有關AI支持的臨床推理訓練的研究。
